subject: Vector compatibility checklist & SDK quickstart — Halcyon Commerce POC
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@halcyoncommerce.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@halcyoncommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Vector compatibility checklist & SDK quickstart — Halcyon Commerce POC

Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet you both on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum for the POC:

Summary of what we heard
- Use case: semantic search + rerank for product search and “related items” widgets.
- Current vectors: vendor X embeddings (1024-d), stored in their managed vector DB.
- Target latency: 75–150ms 95th for search queries.
- Volume: ~250QPS peak for search paths, batch update jobs nightly.

Key integration points we should resolve in the POC
1) Vector dimensionality compatibility
   - Options: (A) adopt 1024 where possible, (B) re-embed to Redwood-verified 768 model to reduce cost/latency.
   - Tradeoffs: re-embedding improves latency & lower storage, but requires migration window and quality validation.
2) Batching & inference throughput
   - Suggest starting with batch_size=32 for bulk re-embed jobs; continuous query batching can be 8–16 depending on latency SLO.
3) Normalization scheme
   - Recommend L2 normalization for cosine similarity; we can run a small A/B against unnormalized vectors.
4) Migration approaches (high-level)
   - Cold reindex: re-embed entire corpus during a single migration window (fastest to consistent results).
   - Rolling re-embed: keep existing vectors operational; re-embed on read/write, prioritize hot items.
   - Dual-index: keep vendor index as fallback and run traffic-splitting for quality checks.
5) Auth & SDK quickstart
   - We support API key and mTLS for Private deployments. For the POC we recommend API key scoped to the POC project.
   - Attached: lightweight SDK snippet for Python + curl examples.
6) Routing & fallback
   - Route low-latency queries to our optimized 768 model; fallback to vendor index or larger model only on error.
7) Reranker & structured output
   - We can chain generation/rerank: candidate retrieval -> reranker model call -> structured JSON output for the UI.

Immediate asks from you
- Confirm whether you prefer a cold reindex or rolling re-embed approach for the POC.
- Share a small sample of product metadata (500 rows) and a snippet of an existing vector file (anonymized) so we can run compatibility checks.
- Confirm legal/compliance contact for SOC2 artifacts if you need hosted vs dedicated isolation.

Proposed next steps / timeline
- This week: compatibility smoke test (we run similarity checks on sample vectors) — target Wed 17 Jun.
- Next week: deploy SDK quickstart to a Halcyon dev project and run a 2-day load test.
- Week after: migration approach decision + kickoff migration job.

Attachments included: halcyon-vector-playbook.pdf (migration playbook), redwood-sdk-quickstart-snippet.txt (tiny code examples).

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa and Karthik for the technical handoff.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@halcyoncommerce.com>

Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@halcyoncommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vector compatibility checklist & SDK quickstart — Halcyon Commerce POC

Sean — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with engineering: 

- We prefer a rolling re-embed for now to minimize risk (hot items first).
- Current vectors are 1024-d, float32, stored in vendor X. We can export a CSV of 1,000 anonymized vectors for the smoke test.
- For normalization: we normally use L2, but one of our ML engineers wants to test no-normalize + dot product for legacy scoring. Would be great if Redwood can run both for comparison.
- Auth: API key is fine for the dev POC. For production we’ll need KMS-integrated key rotation; can you point us to your Private deployment mTLS doc?

Questions:
1) What is the expected storage delta if we move from 1024->768 with quantization (INT8) — ballpark estimate?
2) Can we do partial rerank (top-50 candidates only) to cut cost?
3) Does Redwood's SDK auto-manage KV cache for rerankers or do we need to implement a caching layer?

We’ll upload the sample vectors to the Drive link you shared by EOD. Looking forward to the smoke test.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Search Engineering, Halcyon Commerce
alex.rivera@halcyoncommerce.com

Subject: Re: Vector compatibility checklist & SDK quickstart — Halcyon Commerce POC

Looping in the technical team notes and suggested owners: 
- Karthik: own migration plan + migration job orchestration (rolling re-embed flow).
- Laura: run normalization A/B and evaluate recall/precision lift.
- I’ll own the POC timeline and report back on performance SLOs.

Quick answers to Alex’s Qs: 
1) Storage delta (very rough): 1024 float32 ~= 4KB per vector. 768 INT8 quantized ~= 768 bytes per vector. So roughly ~5–6x storage reduction with INT8. We’ll validate exact numbers on the sample set.
2) Partial rerank: yes — we recommend top-50 candidates for reranker stage for cost/latency tradeoff; we’ll include config knobs in the playbook.
3) KV cache: Redwood runtime manages KV cache for generation/rerank sessions automatically; you can also add a Redis cache in front if you want cross-request pooling for cold starts.

Action items I’ll take now:
- Kick off compatibility smoke test when Alex uploads sample vectors.
- Prepare two small eval prompts (product search + related items) for A/B.
- Draft the rolling re-embed job steps (pre-checks, throttles, cutover).

—Marissa
